summary: Physics Lab source currently has no pure invariant proving that PhysicsLabRecipe.RESOLVED_REGION.canonicalContentKeys exactly matches the realized PhysicsLabRecipe.build().entities key set. The resolved fingerprint/repro identity can therefore drift out of semantic alignment with the physical lab recipe if an entity key is added/removed/renamed without synchronizing canonicalContentKeys (or vice versa). Existing physics_lab_recipe coverage checks a hard-coded required entity set, and physics_lab_resolved_identity replays the already-locked canonicalContentKeys, but neither cross-checks the two sets. This fits the active HG-BACKFILL-PHYSICS-GEOMETRY test-adversary scope; do not open a duplicate lane.
evidence: src/shared/Physics/PhysicsLabRecipe.luau defines RESOLVED_REGION.canonicalContentKeys independently from the entities returned by build().
tests/physics_lab_recipe.luau verifies a hard-coded requiredKeys table against realized entities but never reads RESOLVED_REGION.canonicalContentKeys.

tests/physics_lab_resolved_identity.luau replays resolved.canonicalContentKeys into ResolvedRegionRecipe.lock(), which proves serialization/replay stability but not correspondence to realized lab content.
A deterministic set-equality regression can be added inside existing HG-BACKFILL-PHYSICS-GEOMETRY write scope, preferably in tests/physics_lab_recipe.luau, with no Studio evidence claim.
